blocks.text: Real Russian sentences that use what the lesson teaches. Type the missing word, or pick it, until it turns green.

These are real sentences: from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English translations, and from the public-domain Russian books in this library, with author and title. Each blank is the word the sentence really has; the word in brackets is its dictionary form.

exercises.why: «The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative.» «To say 'There isn't …' we use the word нет followed by the genitive case.» — DLI, Lesson 27; Wikibooks.

exercises.prompt: They are trying to cozy up to imperialist forces in order to achieve their political aims.
exercises.why: «The person or thing feared is in the Genitive case: Я боюсь этого человека.» «The object (of ждать) is in the accusative case if animate and in the genitive case if inanimate.» — DLI, Lessons 27, 66.
